topic: The Wallis Product: An Infinite Dance toward Pi
target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: The Geometric Curiosity
lecture_lines: It is a limit of processes.
Observe a polygon approaching a circle.
animations: Show a circle labeled 'C' with radius 'r' in #FFFFFF.
Introduce the constant pi as the ratio limit.
Fade all elements, focus on pi in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Sine Integral
lecture_lines: This leads to the Wallis formula.
animations: Display the integral of sin(x) from 0 to pi.
Visualize the area under the curve in #0000FF.
Explain how this integral relates to Wallis product.

sections.title: The Derivation: Linking Ratios to Pi
lecture_lines: Analyze the ratio of consecutive integrals.
This isolates Pi in the limit.
animations: Show the sequence of integrals 'I_n' for n.
Highlight the relationship between 'I_n' and pi.
Show the transition of ratio to infinite product.
Display the convergence of terms to pi/2.

sections.title: The Wallis Formula Revealed
lecture_lines: Pi over two is a product.
animations: Write the Wallis formula clearly in #FFFFFF.
Show the limit as n approaches infinity in #FF00FF.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Elegance of Infinity
lecture_lines: Wallis product connects integers to circles.
animations: Display the final elegant infinite product for pi.
Visualize terms approaching value with pulses in #FFFFFF.
Summarize the discovery with 'Pi' centered in #FFFF00.
